grades.quote: terminate all previously-launched speculative executions of the addresstranslation algorithm (for the specified ASID, if applicable)
grades.reason: Only passing mentions of the ASID in the context of SFENCE.VMA and speculative page-table walks. It does not explain how the ASID identifies an address space or how SFENCE.VMA selects translations by ASID.

grades.quote: If the new address space’s page tables have been modified, or if an ASID is reused, it may be necessary to execute an SFENCE.VMA instruction
grades.reason: This is the satp passage. It links ASID reuse and SFENCE.VMA, and says writing satp does not flush translation caches, which is why a large ASID space reduces context-switch cost. It never describes the ASID field layout or says the ASID identifies an address space.

grades.quote: the fence orders all reads and writes made to any level of the page tables, but only for the address space identified by integer register _rs2_ .
grades.reason: Explains how SFENCE.VMA uses the ASID in rs2. With rs1=x0 and rs2≠x0, it fences only the address space identified by rs2, leaves global mappings unordered, and invalidates matching cached translations. It also covers the rs1≠x0, rs2=x0 case, which applies to all address spaces. It says nothing about the satp ASID field, so it answers only the SFENCE.VMA half.

grades.quote: the fence orders only reads and writes made to leaf page table entries corresponding to the virtual address in _rs1_ , for the address space identified by integer register _rs2_ .
grades.reason: Covers the SFENCE.VMA case with rs1≠x0 and rs2≠x0, where the fence is limited to the address space identified by rs2. It also explains how ASID bits in rs2 are handled (reserved bits above ASIDMAX, bits ignored when ASIDLEN<ASIDMAX). This is useful for SFENCE.VMA's ASID use, but it doesn't describe the satp ASID field.
